entries.name: Windows 11
entries.notes: Official Microsoft media, fetched on demand. Edition, local-account vs OOBE, and debloat are options.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Disk 0 is wiped without prompting. On unsupported hardware, enable 'skip requirement checks'.

entries.name: Windows Server 2025 (Desktop Experience)
entries.notes: The server with the familiar Windows desktop on it, and Server Manager. 180-day evaluation media, fetched from Microsoft on demand and convertible to licensed afterwards.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Disk 0 is wiped without prompting.
entries.import_from: your volume-licensing portal, for licensed rather than evaluation media

entries.name: Windows Server 2025 (Server Core)
entries.notes: No desktop and no Server Manager: administered from another machine, or from a command line on the console. Smaller and with less to patch. The same ISO as the Desktop Experience entry, so having one means the other is already downloaded — but the choice cannot be changed after installation, and evaluation Server Core cannot be converted to licensed later.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Disk 0 is wiped without prompting.
entries.import_from: your volume-licensing portal, for licensed rather than evaluation media

entries.name: Windows Server 2022 (Desktop Experience)
entries.notes: The previous LTSC, for hardware or applications not yet cleared for 2025, with the familiar Windows desktop on it. Also 180-day evaluation media.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Disk 0 is wiped without prompting.
entries.import_from: your volume-licensing portal, for licensed rather than evaluation media

entries.name: Windows Server 2022 (Server Core)
entries.notes: The previous LTSC with no desktop and no Server Manager, administered from another machine or a command line. The same ISO as the Desktop Experience entry; the choice cannot be changed after installation.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Disk 0 is wiped without prompting.
entries.import_from: your volume-licensing portal, for licensed rather than evaluation media

entries.name: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Server
entries.notes: Boots the Ubuntu Server installer. (Zero-touch autoinstall is available in a workspace recipe.)
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Secured-core PCs need the 3rd-party UEFI CA enabled in firmware for Secure Boot.

entries.name: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Desktop
entries.notes: Boots the live desktop; install from there. The current LTS.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Secured-core PCs need the 3rd-party UEFI CA enabled in firmware for Secure Boot.

entries.name: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Server
entries.notes: Boots the Ubuntu Server installer. The current LTS.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Secured-core PCs need the 3rd-party UEFI CA enabled in firmware for Secure Boot.

entries.name: Fedora 44 Workstation
entries.notes: Boots the Fedora live desktop; install from there.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Signed shim, so Secure Boot works out of the box on most firmware.

entries.name: Debian 13 (netinst)
entries.notes: Small network installer — the target machine needs wired internet during setup.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Signed shim, so Secure Boot works out of the box on most firmware.

entries.name: Arch Linux
entries.notes: Boots the Arch installer environment; run archinstall or install by hand.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Unsigned — Secure Boot must be off.

entries.name: Fedora 44 Server
entries.notes: Full server install DVD — no network needed during setup.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Signed shim, so Secure Boot works out of the box on most firmware.

entries.name: NixOS 26.05 (minimal)
entries.notes: Console installer for the declarative, reproducible distro. Install from its shell.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Unsigned — Secure Boot must be off.

entries.name: Omarchy
entries.notes: Opinionated Arch + Hyprland desktop, preconfigured and ready to use.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Unsigned — Secure Boot must be off.

entries.name: CachyOS Desktop
entries.notes: Arch, tuned for speed: optimised packages and a custom kernel, with a graphical installer.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Unsigned — Secure Boot must be off.

entries.name: CachyOS Handheld
entries.notes: For handheld gaming PCs — Steam Deck, ROG Ally, Legion Go. Boots straight into a game session.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Unsigned — Secure Boot must be off.

entries.name: SteamOS (Steam Deck recovery)
entries.notes: Valve's recovery image, for Steam Deck hardware only — reinstalls or repairs SteamOS on a Deck. Not a SteamOS installer for a PC; for handheld gaming PCs generally, see CachyOS Handheld.
entries.firmware_notes: Boot a powered-off Deck with Volume-Down held to pick this stick. Unsigned — Secure Boot must be off.

entries.name: Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit)
entries.notes: For Raspberry Pi hardware, not a PC. Writes a ready-to-run system — no installer to sit through.
entries.firmware_notes: Boots on Pi 3/4/5 and Zero 2. A Pi 4 or 5 boots this from USB; earlier boards want an SD card.

entries.name: Pop!_OS 24.04
entries.notes: System76's desktop, with their COSMIC environment. Intel/AMD build.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Secured-core PCs need the 3rd-party UEFI CA enabled in firmware for Secure Boot.

entries.name: Bazzite
entries.notes: Fedora Atomic built for gaming — Steam, controllers and drivers ready on first boot. Good on handhelds and desktops alike.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Signed shim, so Secure Boot generally works.

entries.name: Nobara 44
entries.notes: Fedora with the codecs, drivers and gaming tweaks already applied — NVIDIA and OBS work out of the box.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Unsigned kernel — Secure Boot must be off.

entries.name: Garuda Linux (Dr460nized)
entries.notes: Arch made comfortable: a heavily themed KDE Plasma desktop with its own installer and maintenance tools.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. No signed shim in the image — Secure Boot must be off to boot this stick.

entries.name: PikaOS 4 (Nest, GNOME)
entries.notes: Debian Sid tuned for gaming. GNOME desktop; a separate NVIDIA build exists upstream.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Needs an x86-64-v3 CPU (Haswell/Excavator or newer). Unsigned — Secure Boot must be off.

entries.name: openSUSE Tumbleweed
entries.notes: SUSE's rolling release, with YaST and snapshot-based rollback.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Signed shim, so Secure Boot generally works.

entries.name: Proxmox VE 9.2
entries.notes: Bare-metal hypervisor: KVM virtual machines and LXC containers, managed from a web console.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Installs Debian underneath and takes the whole disk.

entries.name: TrueNAS (SCALE)
entries.notes: Storage appliance OS — ZFS, shares and apps. Installs to its own boot device, separate from the pool disks.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Wants a dedicated boot drive; your data disks stay untouched.

entries.name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10
entries.notes: Download it yourself — Red Hat puts its images behind an account, so there is no link to pin. For the same packages with no account, see AlmaLinux or Rocky Linux.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Signed shim, so Secure Boot works.
entries.import_from: https://access.redhat.com/downloads (a no-cost Developer subscription covers it)

entries.name: AlmaLinux 10.2
entries.notes: RHEL 10, rebuilt and free. Minimal install set — extra package groups want a network or the DVD image.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Signed shim, so Secure Boot generally works.

entries.name: Rocky Linux 10.2
entries.notes: The other RHEL 10 rebuild, under community governance. Minimal install set, same as AlmaLinux above.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot. Signed shim, so Secure Boot generally works.

entries.name: Linux Mint 22.1 (Cinnamon)
entries.notes: Boots the Linux Mint live desktop; install from there.
entries.firmware_notes: UEFI boot.
